name: agy

detect.detect_notes: `agy --version` prints a bare semver ("1.1.28", live 2026-09-10). On this machine agy is a single native agy.exe directly on PATH (no npm shim, no script wrapper), so detect.npm_exe/npm_entry do not apply: the PATH scan resolves the .exe and spawns it without a shell. The binary self-updates in place (1.1.27 -> 1.1.28 observed 2026-09-09 probe report); version drift policy applies — re-run probes after upgrades.

command.mode_args_notes: agy has no --permission-mode; the agent-execution axis is `--mode` (help 1.1.28 lists accept-edits|plan; no flag = default). Live 2026-09-10 native zero-copy probe (tmp/agy-native-probe/out/): plan headless auto-denies write_file even with ZERO permission rules (t2a: file absent, result.denied_actions[write_file], exit 0) — a true enforced read-only tier. accept-edits auto-approves write_file when no rule governs it (t2c), so write SCOPING comes from the user's native ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json permissions (allow write_file(<root>) + ask write_file(*); verified both directions t3-in/t3-out). paidan never writes that file (invariant 4): the rules are user-maintained native config; without them workspace-write is unscoped and shell.exec auto-denies. unattended shares accept-edits; its shell.exec requirement rides the native command(*) allow rule (verified t6c). --sandbox is deliberately absent: on Windows 1.1.28 it adds an unsandboxed(*) gate that headless can never grant (t6b auto-deny) and its readwrite mount config rejects drive-stripped rule paths — the native permission engine is the enforcement layer.
command.argv_notes: Prompt rides argv (-p <prompt>) like the suite adapter (prompt_transport=argv); there is no single-shot stdin text mode (--input-format stream-json is a multi-turn NDJSON protocol, out of v0 scope). Windows command-line budget applies to the prompt bytes (suite cap 26 KiB). --print-timeout is always passed: native default is 5m, window 30s..120m; 30m preserves the historical operational envelope. 1.1.28 timeout semantics: partial output + exit 0 + status SUCCESS + stderr marker, surfaced as the print-timeout-partial-output refusal signal. Native config (~/.gemini) decides auth and default model; paidan never stages or overrides beyond the flags above.

env._env_notes: AGY_CLI_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true is pinned (same as the suite): without it, headless runs still touched the native updater (update_status.json flipped to 'Update failed, please install from website', last_check.timestamp refreshed; live 2026-09-10) even though antigravity-cli/settings.json carries update.mode=none; with the env var, updater files stay untouched (verified). HOME/USERPROFILE are NOT set: agy runs against the user's real ~/.gemini (zero-copy native home; Google OAuth lives in the OS keyring, unaffected by HOME isolation). Paidan never stages or copies agy config/credentials.

fs.read.via: view_file requires a native read_file allow rule (request-review default auto-denies it headless, verified 2026-09-10); on Windows 1.1.28 only the unscoped form read_file(*) matched — every scoped path form tested (drive-stripped dir, dir/*, full-drive, backslash) failed to authorize view_file, an upstream limitation to revisit on upgrades. grep_search/list_dir work unlisted. Production native settings carry read_file(*).

fs.write.via: workspace-write = --mode accept-edits + native allow write_file(*). CALIBRATED 2026-09-10 on agy 1.2.0 (self-update from 1.1.28): scoped write_file allow rules stopped matching on Windows — 4-variant live test (unscoped glob / drive-letter glob / exact dir / drive-letter exact) showed ONLY unscoped write_file(*) authorizes writes; 1.1.28-era scoped rules (drive-stripped official normalization) are inert under 1.2.0, same limitation class as read_file. Consequence: on Windows 1.2.0 write governance is whole-disk within accept-edits; the old out-of-scope auto-deny (t3-out) is no longer expressible via scoped rules. read-only = --mode plan still auto-denies all writes headless even rule-free (t2a; P2 probe pass on 1.2.0). deny write_file(*) beats accept-edits auto-approval (t2b, 1.1.28). Native settings are user-maintained; paidan never writes them (invariant 4).

shell.exec.via: run_command auto-approved headless when the native allow rule command(*) is present (verified 2026-09-10: output captured, DONE, no denial); without the rule it auto-denies (request-review + no prompt channel). SOFT because shell is NOT path-confined without --sandbox: on 2026-09-10 a workspace-write run's shell leg wrote a duplicate deliverable into the paidan CALLER's cwd (outside the run cwd; run_command starts from an inherited PWD-ish directory on Windows — the suite documented this as 'run_command may start from C:\'); write_file tool writes stay natively path-governed, shell writes are not. Under --sandbox run_command demands an unsandboxed grant headless runs can never receive — paidan does not pass --sandbox.

net.fetch.via: read_url_content tool exists and the native allow rule read_url(*) is in place, but no live fetch probe was run in the 2026-09-10 native matrix; 1.1.28 changed URL fetching to default-Ask (probe report 2026-09-09 §8), so expect auto-deny without the rule

interact.ask.via: headless has no approval channel: every ask/unlisted action is auto-denied and lands in result.denied_actions with the stderr jetski line (verified repeatedly 2026-09-10); ask write_file(*) is exactly this backstop

permission.presets_notes: Mapping: read-only=--mode plan (write/exec auto-deny headless, in-band evidence), workspace-write=--mode accept-edits (+ native allow write_file(*)), unattended=--mode accept-edits (+ native command(*) rule for shell.exec). Enforcement is carried by the user's native ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json permissions — user-maintained native config that paidan never writes. Windows 1.2.0 caveat: write_file rules only match unscoped (*), so workspace-write is whole-disk within the file tool (scoped path rules are inert); run_command shell egress was never path-confined (shell.exec=soft). Unattended submits therefore carry a soft warning.

denial_evidence.via: three in-band channels, all live-verified 2026-09-10: (1) result.denied_actions[] e.g. {action:write_file,display_name:WriteToFile} for ask/plan auto-denies; (2) step_update state=ERROR tool_info.error TOOL_ERROR messages ('permission check failed ... Matches user-configured deny rule', 'user denied permission ...') for explicit rules; (3) stderr 'jetski: no output produced — a tool required the "<action>" permission ... auto-denied'. Empty response with SUCCESS is a legal terminal shape and stays evidence, not automatic failure

resume.notes: Session handle = conversation_id (UUID) from the init/result events. Cross-process resume via --conversation <id> verified 2026-09-10 (1.1.28): recalled prior content exactly, and resolution is machine-wide — the same id resumed from a DIFFERENT cwd too (supersedes the 2026-09-09 probe report's cwd-scoped assumption for explicit ids). --continue/-c picks the most recent conversation of the current cwd (verified). mode_args are re-spliced on resume (no resume_argv): --mode and --conversation coexist in one argv (suite adapter shape; a resumed run re-tiers from the new invocation). Concurrent resume of the same conversation was not probed; treat as forbidden (transcript interleaving, claude-analog).

models.notes: `agy models` (headless-safe, verified 2026-09-10) prints TSV <id>\t<Display Name>; 14 ids under the google-oauth (OS keyring) connection: gemini-3.8/3.7/3.6-flash-{high,medium,low}, gemini-3.1-pro-{high,low}, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6-thinking, gpt-oss-120b-medium. The catalog varies with auth method: modelProvider=gemini + GEMINI_API_KEY dual-config is a documented second connection (probe report 2026-09-09 §4) but UNVERIFIED here (no key on this machine; paidan never does cross-connection fallback). Selection = config.json defaults.model -> --model; absent, agy's native default (antigravity-cli/settings.json model display-name key) applies.

parser_notes: stdout NDJSON: init (conversation_id, cwd, permission_mode) -> step_update (agent_response text_delta accumulation; tool ERROR events carry permission TOOL_ERRORs) -> exactly one terminal result (status, response, conversation_id cross-checked against init, usage input/output/cache_read tokens, denied_actions). finalText = result.response, falling back to accumulated agent_response deltas with a warning when no result event arrives. Non-JSON lines, mid-line EOF and conflicting conversation ids degrade the parser. detectRefusals reads the stderr jetski auto-deny line and the 1.1.28 print-timeout marker (partial output + exit 0 + SUCCESS). Evidence: live 1.1.28 captures 2026-09-10 (tmp/agy-native-probe/out/) + suite adapter operations/governance/harnesses/runtime/adapters/agy.mjs.

capabilities._capabilities_notes: No native background for -p runs. Cancel = paidan taskkill tree (v0). Upstream >= 1.1.20 made exit codes semantic (non-zero = cascade failure); print-timeout and soft denials still exit 0 — terminal judgment is evidence-first, never exit-code-only.
